messages.content: i went for a walk with my mother. nothing important happened, but i liked hearing what she saw along the road.
what did she point out to you?
a flower near a wall and a house she used to visit. i had walked past both before and never asked about them.
then the walk gave you her way of seeing a place you already knew. a small detail can carry a story when someone talks about it.
can you keep it about what she saw and said?
you walked a road you knew, but her words helped you see parts of it in a new way.
can you help me write two sentences about it?
i walked with my mother and listened to what she saw along the road. she told me about a flower near a wall and a house she had visited before.
does listened to what she saw sound right?
it is more clear to say listened while she talked about what she saw. seeing and talking are different parts.
write that way.
i walked with my mother and listened while she talked about what she saw. she told me about a flower near a wall and a house she had visited before.
what if i only want one sentence about the good part?
i enjoyed walking a road i knew while my mother told me what she saw and remembered.
use a road i knew.
i enjoyed walking a road i knew while my mother told me what she saw and remembered.
now just a kind reply, not another writing task.
it sounds like a quiet walk that gave you time to know more about her.
write a story about a family visit where no one takes a photo. the child should still remember a small part of it later.

a child visited his aunt with his father on a cold afternoon. they had wanted to stay only a little while, but his aunt had soup ready and asked them to eat before leaving. the child sat near the window with a cup of water. his father and aunt talked about a book they had both read. he did not understand every part, but liked hearing them laugh together. after the meal, his aunt showed him a plant growing near the window. she gave him the name and asked him to look at the shape of one leaf. no one took a photo before they left. later, when someone asked what he remembered about the visit, he talked about the warm soup, the sound of the conversation, and the green leaf by the window. the day had no picture on a phone, but it still had a place in his memory.
can you give the first choice with wanted?
they had wanted to stay only a little while, but his aunt asked them to eat before leaving.
did he need a photo to remember any part?
no. in the story, he remembered sounds, food, and a plant without a photo.
can you say every person will remember a visit the same way?
no. different people can remember different parts and forget other details.
use forget.
people can remember different parts and forget other details.
now tell the memory in his voice with three sentences.
i remember soup at the home of my aunt. i heard my father and aunt talking and having a laugh together. i also remember the green leaf by the window.
what did he not say he remembered?
he did not say he remembered every word of the book conversation.
can you give me an example with this is and another with these are?
this is my book. these are my books.
now make them questions.
is this your book? are these your books?
why did my become your?
because i am now asking you about your books. if you were asking yourself, my could stay.
what if i want to ask whether two books are the same book?
you might mean two objects, or two different words for one object. which meaning do you want?
i mean two people use different words for one book. one says blue book and the other says library book.
then you can ask: do you mean the same book?
what if they say yes?
then this blue book and this library book can be about one object. the two details do not make two books.
now make the original examples about a chair.
this is my chair. these are my chairs.
does these are say all the chairs in the world are mine?
no. it is about the chairs clear in the conversation or the chairs you show.
only give the two questions with chair.
is this your chair? are these your chairs?
i want to ask my brother to turn the music down. write a request, not an order, and do not say he always does something wrong.
could you turn the music down for a little while, please?
add that i am reading a hard page.
i am reading a hard page. could you turn the music down for a little while, please?
what if he asks whether i mean the whole evening?
you can make the time small without giving a minute you have not chosen. just while i work on this page can be clear about the goal.
write the reply only.
just while i work on this page. i will let you know when i am done.
can i say i will be done in five minutes if i do not know?
not for sure. you can say you hope it will be a short time, but you do not know yet.
now he says he can use another room. write a thank you.
thank you. that helps me read clearly.
does that say he has to stop all music?
no. he chose another room so you could read here. that does not make all music wrong.
just say he chose another room.
he chose another room so you could read here. that does not make all music wrong.
write a story about a child starting a book at the last page while thinking it is the first. he should ask why the story is hard to follow.

a child opened a book on the table and began to read. a person in the story was saying goodbye, but he did not know who the person was or what had happened before. he asked his sister why the book began in the middle of a visit. she looked at the page and saw that he was reading the last part first. the book had been left open there. she showed him the front and helped him find the first page. he began again and met the people before the visit was over. this time, the goodbye later in the book had a reason he could follow. he had a laugh at starting from the end, then asked whether someone could choose to read the end first. his sister said some people choose that, but knowing where you begin helps make what you read clear.
can you keep the story simple?

a child began at the last part of a book and did not know what had happened before. his sister showed him the first page. reading from there helped him understand the people and the visit before the goodbye.
what made the first reading hard?
he had started near the end without knowing the people or what happened before.
use things before in the answer.
he did not know the people or the things that had happened before.
now give a question he could ask about the book.
is this the first page of the story?
can the last page be read first in a made up story about someone choosing that?
yes. a story can be told without giving every thing in order. the person reading needs enough context to follow it.
say person reading.
the person reading needs enough context to follow the story, even if it is not told from the first thing to the last.
i asked my friend if she was home, and she just said yes. i kept waiting for more, but that answered the question.
yes. a short answer can be enough when the question is specific and both people know the context.
say enough.
a short answer can be enough when the question is specific and the context is clear.
what if i wanted to know whether she had time to talk too?
then that is another question. being home does not always mean being free to talk.
write the next question simply.
do you have time to talk?
she says a little. what do i know?
she has some time, but it is not clear how much. you can keep the conversation short or ask what works for her.
use not for sure.
you know she has some time, but not a long time for sure. you can ask how much time she has.
just ask it.
how much time do you have?
she says five minutes. give a short reply that does not ask for the whole evening.
five minutes works. thank you for making time.
can i call that too short for everyone?
no. it is the time she has now, not a rule about every conversation.
can you use knew and known with a person name? name is in our words.
i knew her name yesterday. i have known her name for a long time.
does knew always mean i forgot now?
no. knew puts the knowing at a past time, but it does not by itself say you forgot it now.
can have known mean i still know it?
yes. in that simple sentence, it can mean you knew it before and still know it now.
say it without any new example.
you knew it before and still know it now in that example.
use now in a simple explanation.
it can mean you knew it before and still know it now.
now make a sentence where i knew before but forgot.
i knew her name before, but i forgot it.
use forgot.
i knew her name before, but i forgot it.
if i ask you the name, can you make one up to finish the example?
only if you want a made up example. from the sentences alone, i do not know the real name.
only give the sentence where i forgot.
i knew her name before, but i forgot it.
my teacher helped me understand one part of a story. i want to thank her, but i still have questions about the rest.
thank you for helping me understand that part. the rest is still hard for me, but this part is more clear now.
can i leave the hard part out of a thank you?
yes. you do not have to put every open question into the same message.
write it shorter.
thank you for helping me understand that part. it is more clear now.
does that say the whole story is easy?
no. that part keeps the message about the specific help, not every part of the story.
what if i want to ask another question in the same message?
you can add one clear question about the next part, rather than say i still do not understand anything.
can you write the question if i tell you the hard part is why the boy went home?
why did the boy go home at that point in the story?
now put the thanks and question together.
thank you for helping me understand that part. i have one more question: why did the boy go home at that point in the story?
does asking more take away the thanks?
no. you can be happy with one answer and still have another question.
use happy with the help.
you can be happy with the help and still have another question.
write a story about a family playing a new game. one rule should not be clear, and they should look at it together rather than one person choosing all the answers.

a family sat at the table to try a new game. they had a ball, some pieces of paper, and a paper with a rule. at first, one child read it and told everyone where to put things. after they began, the mother asked what happened if two people chose the same piece. the child was not sure. rather than saying the first answer that came to mind was the rule, he put the paper in the middle so everyone could look. they found the part about two people and read it slowly. the father had understood one word in another way, so they tried the example on the paper together. after that, the game was more clear. the child had helped the family start, but did not need to be the only person who understood everything.
can you make it with a game and one paper rule in fewer sentences?

a family tried a new game with a ball and a paper rule. one child helped them start, but was not sure what to do when two people chose the same thing. they looked at the paper together and tried its example. after that, the game was more clear.
did asking a question stop the game for every time after?
no. the question helped them understand the rule and keep playing.
can you give a sentence the child could say when he does not know?
i am not sure. let us look at the paper together.
now make it in our voice as the family.
we were not sure about one rule, so we looked at the paper and tried the example together.
does that mean every person understood every part in the same way?
no. it says they worked on one part that was not clear together. other parts could still be different for each person.
only say what they looked at together.
they looked at the paper rule and its example.
i want to leave a visit early because i am tired. i do not have a work call or another plan. help me say it in a kind way without making something up.
i am tired and would like to go home soon. thank you for having me.
does that keep it about what i told you, without saying i enjoyed it before i gave you that feeling?
yes. it keeps the message about being tired and the wish to go home, with a thank you for the visit.
now i tell you it was good to see the friend. put that in.
it was good to see you. i am tired and would like to go home soon.
does soon tell the person a specific minute?
no. soon gives a general time. if you mean now, it is more clear to say i am going to head home now.
head is in the words, but head home is a different meaning. can you use go?
it was good to see you. i am tired, so i am going to go home now.
can that be kind without saying i will come back tomorrow?
yes. you can give a true reason and a kind goodbye without choosing a next visit.
now only give a shorter message.
it was good to see you. i am going home now because i am tired.
what if i just want a warm last reply from you, not a message?
i hope you get some rest after the visit.
i told someone a thing was true, then learned i had it wrong. i want to change what i said instead of keeping the wrong answer.
you can give the new information and say the first answer was wrong. changing an answer after learning more can be useful, not a reason to keep the wrong one.
can you write a simple message?
i had that wrong before. i learned more, and this is the right information now.
what if i am only less sure, not sure of a new answer?
then say that instead. i am not sure my first answer was right. i need to check before saying it for sure.
can i say i know the right answer just to sound like i can help?
no. you can help by being clear about what you know and what you still need to check.
what if the other person asks why i changed my mind?
you can explain what new detail you learned, or say you found a reason the old answer might not work.
now give a sentence saying the new detail changed my answer, without choosing what the detail is.
i learned a new detail that changed my answer.
does a new detail always make every part of the old answer false?
not always. it may change one part while other parts stay true. you need to look at what the detail changes.
only give the message about not being sure yet again.
i am not sure my first answer was right. i need to check before saying it for sure.
i have a simple way to say it now. i do not want more choices.
okay. we can keep the words you chose.
can you say something kind without another question?
it is good that the message feels more clear to you.
now just goodbye.
goodbye.
with take care, one sentence.
goodbye, and take care.
